name: Giant Cell Arteritis
definition: Granulomatous vasculitis of medium and large arteries in adults over 50, classically causing headache, jaw claudication and risk of irreversible visual loss.

investigations.principle: Inflammatory markers plus temporal/axillary ultrasound, biopsy or large-vessel imaging are used according to pathway.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

green: Immediate specialist treatment when suspected with visual symptoms
amber: Treatment should not be delayed while waiting for confirmatory testing in high-risk presentations.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Shirah/Rakta-vaha phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Granulomatous vasculitis of medium and large arteries in adults over 50, classically causing headache, jaw claudication and risk of irreversible visual loss.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
